newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK DragonAir not to list before CNAC -- paper.
newsitem.headline: HK DragonAir not to list before CNAC -- paper.

text.p: Hong Kong Dragon Airlines Ltd is unlikely to be listed in 1998 unless it is part of a possible listing of its major shareholder, China National Aviation Corp (CNAC), the South China Morning Post said on Sunday.
"The question is whether a listing by the CNAC would include its stake in DragonAir," Henry Fan, managing director of CITIC Pacific Ltd told the newspaper.
Hong Kong Dragonair and CNAC officers were not immediately available for comment.

A separate listing for Dragonair has been rumoured several times, but little progressed seems to have been made. Previous comments from Fan said the listing had been delayed from an intended first quarter 1997 until sometime in 1998.
In January, merchant bankers BZW Asia Ltd told Reuters that CNAC was considering a listing on the Hong Kong stock exchange as one of the options being considered as a means of raising financing.
CNAC is the commercial operating arm of China's aviation regulator, the Civil Aviation Authority of China (CAAC).
In April 1996, CNAC bought 17.66 percent of Dragonair from Swire Pacific Ltd and Cathay Pacific Airways, and another 17.66 percent from CITIC Pacific.
Swire and Cathay jointly hold about 26 percent of Dragonair following the sale of shares to CNAC, and CITIC holds 28 percent.
The stake in Dragonair may be the largest asset held by CNAC's Hong Kong arm, analysts told the paper.
Dragonair reported pre-tax profits of HK$267 million in 1995 and an estimated HK$307 million in 1996.
